IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: We regularly inspect electrical equipment in your area to help keep your electricity supply safe and reliable. As part of this programme, we will be replacing and upgrading 25 electricity poles. These poles play an important role in helping us deliver a safe and reliable supply to homes and businesses. This work will also reduce the likelihood of unexpected power cuts in the future as we appreciate that some customers may have experienced unplanned power cuts in the last 6 months. To maintain your electricity supply during the work, we'll temporarily connect your property to a generator. There will be brief interruptions to your power while it is connected and removed. This work is taking place in multiple locations near Hempnall Road, Shotesham Road, Kings Road and Snakes Lane. If you have solar panels, please switch them off to keep them safely isolated. If your system has an 'island mode' (sometimes called backup or standby mode) you can use that instead. This helps prevent any issues during the power cut.

Steps.Message: Hi, I'm Ebony and I am the manager of the text messaging team at UK Power Networks in Ipswich. Today's power cut was unexpected, so we were unable to provide you with prior notice to help you plan ahead. I am pleased to confirm that we managed to resolve this by diverting to get your lights back on as soon as possible. Just so you know, we text customers when we are made aware of problems like this, so if you would like to be notified in the future you can do so here https://UKPN.short.gy/SMS This was a widespread problem on the overhead network and I personally apologise for any disruption this has caused to your day. If you have any questions or are still without power, please call us on 105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Hi, this is Simon from the messaging team at UK Power Networks. I'm sorry for the power cut today; I know the lights going off can be disruptive.

Thanks for your continued patience today. We know a power cut is disruptive, especially with so many people currently working at home. We appreciate this is an added concern, so we want to provide some advice for anyone in this situation.

You can use your phone as a personal hotspot to keep an internet connection (be aware of the data limit your network provider allows for this), use a battery pack to keep your devices charged and adjust the power settings on any laptops or mobile devices to extend their lifespan. As it's quite common for your immediate neighbours to remain on power during an issue like this, ask to see if they can share access to their Wi-Fi network temporarily.

We'll keep you updated.

Sent by Aaron at 23:30 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 08003163105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Logs.Comment:
Sent by Aaron at 23:51 - We can now confirm that all power in the Tunbridge Wells TN3 area should be back on. Our engineers have diverted power around a tree on an overhead cable to get the majority of customers back on. However, due to the location and complexity of the issue, we have also used a temporary generator to restore power to the last of the affected properties. This will provide power until our engineers plan in and safely complete the full repair, which may take a few days.

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

Sent by Aaron at 22:38 - I wanted to reach out to say that our staff are doing everything they can to get your lights back on. Windy weather like we're experiencing now can make things harder for our engineers, especially when trying to repair overhead cabling.

While the weather is impacting our network, damage to our cabling can still occur. Usually, this is due to trees being swayed by the wind and making contact with a cable or piece of pole mounted network equipment, like a transformer.

When this happens, it can create potentially dangerous situations, so if you spot anything wrong with our equipment or cabling, please stay away from the area and call our team on 08003163105, pressing the option for emergencies.

Our engineers are awaiting the arrival of our generator.

Although this will be temporary, engineers will still need to repair the issue before it can be removed and network power is resumed. Depending on the fault, it may take several days for our engineers to pinpoint the problem and plan in the work. The temporary generator will remain on site to provide power until we can locate the issue and restore the network back to normal running conditions.

If you'd like any further information, our team are always here to help. Sent by Decasta at 21:05.

Steps.Message:
Sent by Dray at 20:31 - We want to reassure you that we've not forgotten about you and we know that the estimated time frame has passed. I apologise for any confusion or inconvenience caused by the delay in restoring the power.

As our staff are working with live electricity, we need to wait until it is safe for them to stop and contact us with an update.

Our engineers have let us know that due to the complexity of the repairs, power restoration has taken longer than expected. To give them time to do this safely, the estimated time frame to restore your power is now between 20:30 & 21:30.

If you are worried about anyone who may be more vulnerable in your property who is affected by the outage today please don't hesitate to call us free on: 0800 316 3105
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Sent by Theo at 02:17 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

With high winds, our engineers cannot safely do some of the things they need to, such as climb electricity poles. Added to this, heavy rain can make it difficult to travel and access our equipment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Sent by Aaron at 22:16 - Our engineers have now restored power to all 351 customers in the Maidstone ME15. ME18 area, by removing a tree branch from an overhead cable. We know power may have been off for a long time; we're sorry for any disruption this unplanned power cut caused.  

We know some properties in the area may have faced other recent interruptions, and we're sorry for the extra disruption. Every outage is fully investigated by our engineers, though power may be lost several times before we can safely find and fix the issue. Our customer services team will keep as many customers updated as possible during these investigations.

To talk to us, or let us know that your power isn't restored, call us on 08003163105.

Our engineers have arrived on site in the Maidstone ME15. ME18 area to investigate the power cut affecting 351 properties. 

Specialist engineers are also working to divert power remotely, and this can cause your lights to go on and off. 

We know that a power cut can be very disruptive, even more so if you are vulnerable. If you're worried about an elderly or ill person in your property who is affected by the power cut today, we are able to provide some support. We'll continue to keep you updated with our engineer's progress but for any concerns or questions, don't hesitate to call us free on 08003163105. For more information on how we support vulnerable customers just click here: https://UKPN.short.gy/PSR

Sent by Decasta at 20:20 - Our engineers are on their way. At this point we think the issue is an overhead cabling fault affecting 351 properties.

Specialist engineers from our control room are also working to divert power remotely, so it's possible your power could come back on at any point. We can't always restore everyone this way. That's why we're also sending staff to the area to check our equipment.

Every fault is different, so our time frames have to be estimated but currently we hope to have power back on between 01:00-02:00. We must stress that it may become necessary for this to change, depending on what our engineers find.

We'll keep you updated with our progress.

What will happen next?

This outage affects multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you expect. We're arranging staff to attend ASAP, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting electricity. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to get as many customers back on as we can.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing but we'll always give you the clearest information we have.

Sent by Theo at 03:02 - Just another check in from us, as we know power being off for longer periods can be very disruptive, and we just wanted to help explain why it can take longer to get power restored safely during bad weather like we're having at the moment.

We want to get your power back on as quickly as we can, but the safety of our staff and customers is always our first priority, so we sometimes have to wait until the weather has improved before repairs can begin.

My team and I will continue to keep you updated.

MainMessage: We are currently experiencing problems with the electricity supply in your area.  Our engineers have attended the fault, and have made an emergency repair to restore power to as many premises as possible.  It is our intention to return to make a permanent repair as soon as we can.  I'm sorry, but we can't give you a time for this at present. Please accept our sincere apologies for any inconvenience this may cause.

MainMessage: We have repaired the problem with the electricity supply in your area. Steps.Message:
Sent by Simon at 07:16 - Thanks for your patience over today.

Our engineers have let us know that they have located an area where trees are in contact with our overhead network. We are arranging for additional engineers to head to site to cut away the trees so that they can assess and repair any damage that has been caused to the network.. To give them time to do this safely, the estimated time frame to restore your power is now between 12:30 and 13:30.

We're sorry this is taking longer than expected, and we'll continue to keep you up to date, but if any change to this time comes in from our staff I'll let you know as soon as we hear.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by Simon at 06:13 - Our engineers are in the process of patrolling our overhead cabling and checking the network for any visible problems. They will identify healthy sections of cable which we can try to use to divert power around the fault. Because of this, we're now estimating we'll have the power back on between 09:30-10:30. Further to this, our field staff have just told us that 66 properties now have their power safely back on after making another diversion. I know there's still some properties affected, so I'll keep sending updates but as mentioned, if you're back up and running now, you can always stop receiving SMS messages from us on our website here: https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP. Otherwise, I'll have some more news for you soon.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message:
Hi there. We've just had a shift change, so Simon, Bev, Kevin and Donny are now here to keep you updated with progress from our field teams.

We know it's frustrating being without power, but we wanted to assure you we're still here and as soon as we have some more information we'll update you again.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Sent by Bev at 07:35 - We can now confirm that all power in the Maidstone ME17 area should be back on. Our engineers have diverted power around overhead cable fault to get the majority of customers back on. . However, due to the location and complexity of the issue, we have also used a temporary generator to restore power to the last of the affected properties. This will provide power until our engineers plan in and safely complete the full repair, which may take a few days.

We're really sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused. If your power isn't on or there's anything you'd like to talk to us about, call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Hi. I'm very sorry you're waking to a power cut this morning. A relief team of engineers are now on site. Due to the impact of the high winds and heavy rain from Storm Austen, we're dealing with a lot of power cuts. Our engineers are working 24/7 and are attending each issue as fast as possible. As a guide, we are hoping to have your power restored by 15:00-16:00. We'll continue to provide updates as we get them, however we might not send them as frequently as we would normally. If you have any questions or concerns, please call us on 105. Power back on? We keep texting those signed up and will do until all customers are restored.
